summary: After the broker drops the socket, nothing of the last connection carries over: the first tick after the reconnect has no trade time, and the frame leaves ltt out rather than take the last connection's or pass a receipt time off as one. The next tick with a time brings ltt back, and a partial tick after it keeps that time.

notes: Partial updates overlay within a connection only: docs/port/market-data-frames.md, Partial-update feeds; lead correction 2026-11-09, .lane/107/decisions.md: a field a partial packet omits is unchanged, not unknown. The desktop drops its snapshots on a new connection; the web's Firstock adapter keeps its own (declared).
Lead ruling (round 3 review): on a partial-update feed, no trade time yet in this connection means ltt is left out; a receipt time is never passed off as a trade time.

deviations.reason: The web's Firstock snapshot survives the reconnect, so the first tick of the new connection, which has no i_last_trade_time, goes out with the last connection's trade time: a value from before the outage presented as current. The desktop starts each connection afresh and, with no trade time yet on it, leaves ltt out rather than pass a receipt time off as one.

deviations.reason: The web sends Firstock's trade time in epoch seconds as ltt, where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds; the desktop sends ms.

deviations.reason: The web's Quote sends oi 0 for an equity whose tick carries no open interest (data.get("i_open_interest", 0)); a value the broker did not send is left out, never sent as 0 (docs/api/websocket-streaming/quote.md, web openalgo#2376). The desktop's Quote leaves it out.
